title: Feelings dialogue
subject: Arabic
unit: Spring 2: Common vocabulary: personal pronouns, my family, adjectives and moods
source: Seeded from arabic/y7 lesson 20 (Pupil PDF worksheet: feelings dialogue)
intro: Read the text carefully. Annotate it: underline key words and write your ideas in the margin.

arabic.text:
- السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟
- وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ، بِخَيْرٍ وَالحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ. وَأَنْتِ؟
- أَنَا مُتْعَبَةٌ قَلِيلًا، وَالحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ.

questions.q: Ask a girl how she is, then answer as her (tired).
questions.model: Teacher: to a girl: حَالُكِ (kasrah). Answer: أَنَا مُتْعَبَةٌ, feminine ة.

questions.q: Feelings dialogue on the pupil PDF: write a six-line dialogue between two friends with greetings, كَيْفَ حَالُكَ / حَالُكِ؟ and two feelings, then perform it in a breakout pair.
questions.model: Teacher writes the first two lines and reads them.

questions.q: ask about a third person: كَيْفَ حَالُ أَخِيكَ؟
what does the Sunnah teach to say when angry?
questions.a: Seek refuge in Allah from Shaytan (Bukhari and Muslim): أَعُوذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ.
